html:
The Cuban War of Independence began in February 1895 under the leadership of Jose Marti, Maximo Gomez and Antonio Maceo. Marti was killed in one of the first skirmishes.

The rebels burned cane fields and marched across the whole island to the west. Spain's general Valeriano Weyler answered by forcing rural people into camps, the reconcentration; perhaps 150,000 or more died of hunger and disease. Maceo was killed in 1896.

Reports of Spanish cruelty in American newspapers, and the sinking of the USS Maine in Havana harbour, brought the United States into the war in 1898. The Spanish-American War ended Spanish rule, but Cubans were left out of the peace, and the Platt Amendment limited their independence.
